 Follow Is Election Day a federal holiday? NC voters should make time Nov. 3
 Iris Seaton, Asheville Citizen Times Updated Mon, November 2, 2026 at 5:10 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Is Election Day a federal holiday? NC voters should make time Nov. 3 Election Day is less than 24 hours away, and with the early voting period over , there's only one way left to cast your ballot for most North Carolina residents - in person at your assigned polling place.
 And North Carolina voters will have to make time in their schedules to vote on Election Day.
 This year's early voting dates in North Carolina were Oct. 15-31. During the early voting period, residents could vote at any polling place in their county. Now that the early voting period is over, ballots must be cast on Election Day, during voting hours of 6:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m., and ballots must be cast at a specific assigned polling place.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Here's what to know about time off during Election Day in North Carolina and more.
 When is Election Day?
 Election Day falls on Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polling places open 6:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m. Any voter in line at 7:30 p.m. will be allowed to vote.
 Is Election Day a federal holiday?
 No, Election Day is not a federal holiday.
 Is Election Day a state holiday in NC?
 No, it is not a state holiday in North Carolina.
 Proposed N.C. House Bill 31 could have changed that by increasing the maximum number of paid state holidays from 12 to 13 yearly, with Election Day becoming a paid holiday for state employees. However, the bill has not moved since February 2025, when it was re-referred to the Committee on Election Law.
 Do I get time off from work to vote in North Carolina?
 Not in North Carolina.
 Advertisement Advertisement Forbes explains that 28 states and Washington, D.C. have some form of law that requires employers to allow employees to leave work on Election Day to vote; states include Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Georgia, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, New York, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming.
 What are the other federal holidays left in 2026?
 Remaining federal holidays in 2026 include:
 Wednesday, Nov. 11, Veterans Day
 Thursday, Nov. 26, Thanksgiving Day
 Friday, Dec. 25, Christmas Day
